docs.purpose: Lets a user see and change their notification settings: which kinds of alerts they receive (new leads above a cost threshold, construction phase changes, stalled jobs, urgent start dates) and what time of day they want them delivered.
docs.data_story: It reads 1 table — `user_profiles` and writes `user_profiles`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 5 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `mobile_settings`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Header also cites docs/specs/03-mobile/99_mobile_state_architecture.md §9.14. GET falls back to a hardcoded defaults object when no user_profiles row exists yet, rather than 404/empty. PATCH uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE so a first-ever PATCH creates the row instead of 404ing — a documented behavioural-parity fix versus the old plain UPDATE. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: CENSUS AGREEMENT: census_reads ['user_profiles'] and census_writes ['user_profiles'] both match. FINDING a reviewer must know: the PATCH upsert can CREATE a `user_profiles` row containing only `user_id` plus whatever prefs the client sent (route.ts:122-124) — with NO trade_slug and NO trade_slugs_override. Such a row makes getCurrentUserContext return null (set.length === 0 at src/lib/auth/get-user-context.ts:134-141), so a brand-new user who toggles a notification switch before onboarding gets a profile row that 401s every /api/leads/* route while /api/notifications/preferences keeps working. Second finding: NotificationPrefsSchema is not .strict() (route.ts:24-30) — unknown keys are silently dropped, the opposite of the .strict() convention the leads schemas use (src/features/leads/api/schemas.ts:108). Third: the doc-comment at route.ts:7-9 claims migration 117 flattened these from JSONB; I did NOT verify that against migrations/ — treat it as a claim, not evidence. | Idempotency: Guarded. `INSERT INTO user_profiles (user_id) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET <only the fields the client sent>, updated_at = NOW()` (route.ts:122-124, SET assembled at :106-115). A repeat PATCH with the same body converges to the same column values; `updated_at` is unconditionally refreshed (route.ts:115) with no IS DISTINCT FROM guard, so the timestamp moves on every replay even when nothing changed. Empty payload is a true no-op (route.ts:112-114). | Caching: none observed — no revalidate/dynamic/Cache-Control/unstable_cache in src/app/api/notifications/preferences/route.ts:1-140 | Other guards / classification: Both queries are keyed on the session userId (route.ts:48, :101/:122) — no client-supplied user_id anywhere. The SET clause is assembled from a fixed whitelist of five hard-coded column names (route.ts:106-110) via addField (route.ts:102-105), so the dynamic SQL cannot take a client-controlled identifier; only the VALUES are parameterized placeholders. | Locking tests: src/tests/notifications.infra.test.ts.
